mainTopic: קנסות for blemishing a בכור and cutting off a נגע: how long they last, and whether they pass to a son
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge against רבי אליעזר. He gives an endless קנס to someone who blemishes a בכור, but someone who cuts off his own בהרת only waits until a new נגע appears. רבה and רב יוסף answer that רבי אליעזר is harsh about property, which people are tempted to damage, but not about one's own body. רבא adds that the חכמים also seem inconsistent, and explains that they always penalize the exact act the person did. רב פפא then asks whether רבי אליעזר said 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר', which matters for a חתן who gets a new נגע during his wedding week, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, רבי ירמיה asks whether the קנס on someone who slit a בכור's ear passes to his son after he dies. Two comparisons are set aside. רבי זירא then proves from a field improved during שביעית that the רבנן penalized only the father, not the son. The amud ends as אביי begins a tradition of his own, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The נגעים source that seems to contradict רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about someone who cuts off his בהרת on purpose. There, רבי אליעזר lets him become טהור once a new נגע appears, so his penalty is not forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the white spot got cut off by itself, he is pure. If he cut it off on purpose, רבי אליעזר says he becomes pure once another mark develops. The חכמים say he must wait until the mark spreads over his whole body, or until his spot is smaller than a split bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה about נגעים. It uses this quote to challenge what רבי אליעזר said about the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר says someone who blemishes a בכור is penalized forever, even if a new blemish comes later. Here, someone who cuts off his בהרת on purpose is only penalized until a new נגע appears. So why is רבי אליעזר harsher with the בכור?

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white spot on the skin, one of the signs of צָרַעַת
A mark of צָרַעַת (the skin disease described in the תורה)
Ritually pure
On purpose, intentionally
A split bean; the smallest size of a בהרת that makes a person טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not stated in this section. It was set up just before. The quote itself is the attack: it shows רבי אליעזר giving a penalty that ends, while in the בכור case his penalty never ends.

phrases.english: and it got cut off, he is pure.
phrases.notes: The quote began just before this. It is talking about a person with a בהרת that got cut off by accident.

phrases.english: If he cut it off on purpose,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
when another leprous mark develops on him,
he will become pure from it.
phrases.notes: He means that once the new mark is judged pure, he is also free from the טומאה of the spot he cut off.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
not until it spreads over his whole body,
phrases.notes: When צרעת covers the whole body, the person is טהור (ויקרא 13:12).

phrases.english: or until his white spot is smaller than a split bean!

steps.triggerLanguage: קְצָצָה מִתְכַּוֵּין — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לִכְשֶׁיִּוָּלֵד לוֹ נֶגַע אַחֵר יִטְהַר הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote that the גמרא started before this section, as a challenge to רבי אליעזר's ruling about the בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that someone who blemishes a בכור may never slaughter it, even after a new blemish appears
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the נגעים case, רבי אליעזר lets a new נגע end the penalty of someone who cut off his spot on purpose. So he should also let a new blemish end the penalty in the בכור case.

steps.title: Property versus body
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף answer that רבי אליעזר gives a harsh penalty only where a person's property is involved, not where his body is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: רבי אליעזר penalizes harshly when it is about a person's property, but not when it is about his body.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the answer to the contradiction. The two cases are different kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור is the owner's property, so רבי אליעזר gives a penalty that never ends. The נגע is on the person's own body, so he gives only a limited penalty. This shows רבי אליעזר is consistent: the type of case decides how strict the penalty is.

keyTerms.meaning: Penalizes; gives a קְנָס (a penalty set by the רבנן)
His property or money
His body
Both of them

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
When Rabbi Eliezer penalizes, it is about his property,
about his body he does not penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָנֵיס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, בְּגוּפוֹ לָא קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's penalty for an intentional act should be the same everywhere, so the נגעים ruling contradicts the בכור ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר gives a penalty that never ends only in cases about property. In cases about one's own body, he gives a limited penalty.

steps.title: Why property needs a stronger penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason: a person may well be tempted to blemish his property, but nobody is really tempted to damage his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his property, there is reason to fear he will come to do it. With his body, is there really reason to fear he will come to do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why property and body are treated differently. It finishes the answer of רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is meant to stop people from doing the wrong thing. People are tempted to blemish a בכור so they can use it, so a strong penalty is needed. Cutting into your own skin is painful and unlikely, so a smaller penalty is enough to stop it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is reason to say
That he will come to do it
Is there really reason to say? (a question expecting the answer 'no')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר is consistent. The size of a קנס depends on how tempting the act is. Blemishing one's בכור is tempting, so the penalty never ends. Cutting off one's own בהרת is not very tempting, so a limited penalty is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea about penalties from the רבנן: they are made stronger where people are more likely to sin.

phrases.english: His property: there is reason to say
that he will come to do it,
phrases.notes: Meaning he might really go ahead and blemish his בכור, so a strong penalty is needed to stop him.

phrases.english: His body: is there really reason to say
that he will come to do it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָמוֹנוֹ — אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר דְּאָתֵי לְמֶיעְבַּד, גּוּפוֹ — מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר דְּאָתֵי לְמֶיעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the property-versus-body answer in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction (how tempted a person is)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Why should property get a harsher penalty than the body?
steps.terutzMaskana: People are likely to blemish their own property, so a strong penalty is needed. People are unlikely to cut their own body, so a limited penalty is enough.

steps.title: רבא: The Rabbis seem to contradict themselves too
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that if we ask about רבי אליעזר contradicting himself, we should also ask about the חכמים contradicting themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it only רבי אליעזר's two rulings that seem to clash, while the חכמים's two rulings do not clash?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new problem. The חכמים also seem to rule one way in the case of the בכור and the opposite way in the case of the בהרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the בכור, the חכמים are lenient: once a new blemish appears, the animal may be slaughtered. With the בהרת, the חכמים are strict: a new נגע does not free him, and he stays טמא unless the צרעת spreads over his whole body. That is the same kind of clash we just solved for רבי אליעזר, only in reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: Against, compared with. Used to set one ruling against another.
It is difficult. There is a contradiction.
The חכמים, the majority opinion in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רבי אליעזר is strict with the בכור and lenient with the בהרת. The חכמים are the opposite: lenient with the בכור and strict with the בהרת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Eliezer against Rabbi Eliezer is difficult,
but the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?
phrases.notes: With the בכור the Rabbis allow it after a new blemish, but with the בהרת they keep him טמא forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the contradiction from רבי אליעזר's rulings to the rulings of the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of the חכמים in the משנה about the בכור and the משנה in נגעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים give a limited penalty for the blemished בכור but a permanent penalty for the cut-off בהרת. That looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Both rulings follow one rule: penalize what he did
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי אליעזר is resolved as already explained, and the חכמים are consistent too, because in both cases they penalize the person through the act he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אליעזר against רבי אליעזר is no problem, as we already answered. The חכמים against the חכמים is also no problem. Here they penalized him through what he did, and there they penalized him through what he did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a single principle that explains both rulings of the חכמים. The next step spells out how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not decide the length of the penalty ahead of time. They cancel the very act the person used to get around the law. How long the penalty lasts depends on what that act was.

keyTerms.meaning: As we answered before.
They penalized him (a קנס).
Through what he did.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Eliezer against Rabbi Eliezer is not difficult,
as we answered.
phrases.notes: This is רבה and רב יוסף's answer from before: the strict penalty applies to property, not to one's body.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
here they penalized him in what he did,
and here they penalized him in what he did.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying principle: one rule produces different results in different cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to give a short penalty in one case and a permanent penalty in the other for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: In both cases the חכמים penalize exactly the act the person did, so they are consistent.

steps.title: How the rule plays out with the בכור and the בהרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the principle. With the בכור, only the blemish he made does not count. With the בהרת, his cutting does not count, so he stays טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: By what means did he try to make the בכור permitted? Through this blemish. So the חכמים penalized him in this blemish: it will not make the animal permitted to him. And here too they penalized him in what he did. He meant to make himself טהור through this cutting, so the חכמים penalized him in this cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how 'penalizing what he did' explains each ruling of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בכור case the act was a blemish. Canceling that blemish still leaves room for a later, natural blemish to permit the animal. In the בהרת case the act was the cutting. Canceling the cutting means the נגע is treated as if it were still there, so he stays טמא permanently.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended.
To make it permitted (to slaughter and eat).
A blemish (מום).
Cutting off (here, cutting off the בהרת).
To make himself טהור.

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, a קנס cancels the exact act a person used to get around the law. That is why the penalty is temporary for the בכור and permanent for the בהרת.

phrases.english: By what did he intend to permit it?
By this blemish.
So in this blemish the Rabbis penalized him,
meaning that through this blemish it will not be permitted to him.
And here, they penalized him in what he did:
he intended to make himself pure
through this cutting,
so in this cutting the Rabbis penalized him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the principle stated briefly in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Application of the principle to each case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two penalties of the חכמים look different in strength.
steps.terutzMaskana: The same rule, canceling the act he did, naturally gives a temporary result for the בכור and a permanent one for the בהרת.

steps.title: רב פפא asks how to read רבי אליעזר's word
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the משנה in נגעים quotes רבי אליעזר as saying 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: Did we learn 'יטהר' (he becomes טהור), or did we learn 'ויטהר' (and he becomes טהור)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the exact wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling about the בהרת. It is setting up a discussion of what difference the wording makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said the person becomes טהור when a new נגע appears. The question is whether he becomes טהור right away when the new נגע shows up, or only later, after the new נגע itself is declared טהור. The one-letter difference ('ו') may decide this timing.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a question he wanted resolved).
We learned (in the משנה).
'He will become טהור' versus 'and he will become טהור'.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Did we learn "yit'har" (he will become pure),
phrases.notes: This would mean he becomes טהור from the first נגע as soon as the new one appears.

phrases.english: or did we learn "veyit'har" (and he will become pure)?
phrases.notes: This would mean he stays טמא from the first נגע until the new one is declared טהור.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: יִטְהַר תְּנַן, אוֹ וְיִטְהָר תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the contradiction discussion and turns to the exact wording of רבי אליעזר's ruling about the בהרת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר's word is 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר', which decides when the person becomes טהור from the first נגע.

steps.title: What difference does the wording make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between reading 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא's wording question matters in practice. This sets up the next step, where the difference is shown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the two readings seem to end up the same. Either way, the person is טמא from the new mark until it is declared clean. So the גמרא wants a real case where the two readings give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
'He becomes טהור': the new mark makes him pure from the first mark right away
'And he becomes טהור': he is pure from the first mark only once he is cleared of the new mark

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
phrases.notes: He means: what changes depending on whether the משנה says 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רב פפא's wording question from step 7 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two readings lead to different practical results.

steps.title: The case of a bridegroom who gets a נגע
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up with a חתן who gets a new נגע. A משנה teaches that a חתן is given seven days before his נגע is examined.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for a bridegroom on whom a נגע appeared. As we learned: a bridegroom on whom a נגע appeared is given seven days, for his body, his cloak, and his garment. Similarly, anyone on a festival is given all the days of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference shows up with a חתן. It then quotes a משנה: a חתן is not examined by a כהן during his seven wedding days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the כהן has not yet looked at a new mark, it cannot make the person טמא. So during the wedding week, the only question is whether he is still טמא from the first mark he cut off. That is exactly where 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר' differ.

keyTerms.meaning: A bridegroom
A צרעת mark
A cloak
A garment
A pilgrimage festival

phrases.english: For a bridegroom on whom a נגע appeared.
As we learned in a משנה:
A bridegroom on whom a נגע appeared,
they give him seven days,
whether the mark is on him, his cloak, or his garment,
and similarly on a festival,
they give him all the days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by naming a case where the readings differ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of a חתן who gets a new נגע during his seven-day grace period.

steps.title: If the reading is 'יטהר', the חתן is fully pure
steps.stepSummary: With the reading 'יטהר', the new mark already freed him from the first mark. The new mark is not examined yet, so he is completely טהור during the wedding week.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learned 'יטהר', then he is already pure from the first mark. For the second mark, we wait seven days of feasting for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the first reading. With 'יטהר', the חתן is completely טהור during his wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יטהר' means that as soon as the new mark appears, the old טומאה from the cut-off mark ends. The new mark is not judged until after the seven days. So during the wedding week, nothing is making him טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the first one (the first mark)
For the latter one (the new mark)
The seven days of wedding feasting

phrases.english: If you say we learned 'יטהר',
then he has already become pure from the first mark,
and for the latter mark we wait for him
the seven days of feasting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חתן case to the reading 'יטהר'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With 'יטהר', the חתן is fully טהור during his wedding week.

steps.title: If the reading is 'ויטהר', the חתן is still impure
steps.stepSummary: With the reading 'ויטהר', the first mark's טומאה lasts until he is cleared of the new mark. So the grace period does not help him; he stays טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say we learned 'ויטהר', then in the end, even though he does not become impure from the second mark, he is still standing impure from the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the second reading. With 'ויטהר', the חתן is still טמא during his wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ויטהר' means the first טומאה ends only once he is declared clean from the new mark. That cannot happen until the new mark is examined, which is after the seven days. So the old טומאה stays the whole week.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; either way
He is standing in a state of טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: With 'יטהר', the חתן is טהור during his wedding week. With 'ויטהר', he is still טמא from the first mark.

phrases.english: But if you say we learned 'ויטהר',
in the end,
even though he does not become impure from the latter mark,
he is still standing impure from the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the difference begun in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With 'ויטהר', the חתן stays טמא from the first mark.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reading is correct and leaves it as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final answer to רב פפא's question and admits there is none. It ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the difference is real, but no source decides between 'יטהר' and 'ויטהר'. So the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: What is the answer? Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question from step 7 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not know whether רבי אליעזר said 'יטהר' or 'ויטהר', so the status of the חתן during his wedding week stays unresolved.

steps.title: Does the penalty pass to the son?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the קנס on a man who slit the ear of a בכור continues on his son after the father dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: if someone slits the ear of a בכור and then dies, do we penalize his son after him?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי ירמיה wants to know if the קנס on the father is passed down to his son once the father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who deliberately makes a מום in a בכור is penalized: he may not slaughter it because of that מום. The question is whether this קנס belongs only to the person who sinned, or whether it stays on the animal even after it passes to his heir.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces a real question)
Slits the ear, which makes a מום on purpose
A firstborn animal, holy for a כהן
To penalize (a קנס from the רבנן)

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
One who slits the ear of a firstborn and dies,
what is the law about penalizing his son after him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תיקו about the חתן in step 12 and returns to our משנה's case of someone who slits the ear of a בכור, now asking whether the קנס passes to his son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the קנס on someone who made a מום in a בכור carries over to his son after his death.

steps.title: The case of selling a slave to gentiles does not settle it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of a man who sold his עבד כנעני to גוים, where the son is penalized, and explains why that case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn from someone who sold his slave to gentiles and died, where the son was penalized, that won't work. There, every single day the slave is kept from doing מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible source for the answer and pushes it away. In that case the son is penalized, but for a reason that does not apply to a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slave sold to גוים, the damage keeps happening every day, because the slave cannot keep his מצוות. So the son must fix the problem too. With the בכור, there is no ongoing harm like that, so we cannot learn from the slave case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (bringing a possible comparison)
One who sells his עבד כנעני to גוים
Keeps him from doing מצוות

phrases.english: If you would say [to learn from]:
one who sells his slave to gentiles and dies
they penalized his son after him,
[that is different,] because each and every day
he keeps him from מצוות.
phrases.notes: An עבד כנעני is obligated in many מצוות, and in a גוי's house he can't keep them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible source that would say yes, the son is penalized, and sets it aside.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning from the slave case to the בכור case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The slave case has an ongoing daily harm (missing מצוות) that the בכור case lacks.

steps.title: The case of planned work on חול המועד does not settle it either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of someone who planned his work for חול המועד and died, where the son is not penalized, and explains why that case is also different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn from someone who planned his work for חול המועד and died, where the son was not penalized, that won't work either. There, the father never actually did anything forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a second possible source, this one pointing the other way, and pushes it away as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חול המועד case the father only planned. He died before doing any forbidden act, so there is nothing to punish the son for. The man who slit the ear of the בכור actually did a forbidden act, so this case cannot answer our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Planned his work on purpose (to fall at a certain time)
חול המועד, the middle days of a יום טוב
A forbidden act

phrases.english: If you would say [to learn from]:
one who planned his work for the Festival's middle days and died
they did not penalize his son after him,
[that is different,] because he never did the forbidden act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a second possible source, one that would say no, the son is not penalized, and sets it aside too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning from the חול המועד case to the בכור case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the חול המועד case no forbidden act was done. In the בכור case one was.

steps.title: Was the penalty on the man or on his property?
steps.stepSummary: Since neither comparison works, the גמרא states the real question: did the רבנן penalize the man himself, or his property?
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the law here? Did the רבנן penalize him personally, and he is gone? Or did they penalize his property, and that is still here?
steps.whatsHappening: After setting aside both comparisons, the גמרא lays out the two clear sides of the question about the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קנס was on the person, it ends when he dies, and the son may slaughter the animal. If the קנס was on the animal as his property, it stays with the animal even in the son's hands. רבי זירא answers this in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what is the law?
On him personally
On his property
He is not here / it is still here

steps.whatToRemember: The question boils down to this: is a קנס on the person, ending at his death, or on the property, staying with the son?

phrases.english: Here, what is the law?
Did the Rabbis penalize him himself, and he is no longer here,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְמָמוֹנֵיהּ קְנַסוּ רַבָּנַן, וְהָא אִיתֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps the Rabbis penalized his property, and that is still here?
phrases.notes: The property is the בכור itself, which is now with the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both comparisons fail, the גמרא returns to the question from step 13 and sharpens it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the קנס for making a מום in a בכור is on the person or on his property.

steps.title: רבי זירא points to a משנה about a field in the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי ירמיה the answer was already taught. He quotes a משנה: a field that was only cleared of thorns during שביעית may be planted after שביעית, but a field that was fertilized or used as an animal pen may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this. A field whose thorns were cleared during שביעית may be planted when שביעית ends. If it was fertilized, or animals were kept on it, it may not be planted when שביעית ends.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins his answer to the question from step 16 by quoting a משנה. This step lays out the case, and the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing thorns is a small act, so no penalty applies. Fertilizing the field or penning animals on it really improves the land, so the רבנן penalized the owner by not letting him plant it right after שביעית. This gives us a clear case of a קנס that we can test against the question about the son.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a משנה or ברייתא)
The seventh year, when the land must rest
Its thorns were cleared
It was improved (fertilized)
It was used as an animal pen, so the animals' manure fertilized it
The year right after שביעית ends

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is answering רבי ירמיה. The source is a משנה in שביעית 4:2.

phrases.english: A field whose thorns were cleared during the seventh year
may be sown after the seventh year ends.
If it was improved, or used as an animal pen,
it may not be sown after the seventh year ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 16 (does the קנס apply to the person or to his property?) by bringing a parallel case of a קנס.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a rabbinic קנס on a person passes on to his son after he dies.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is found in a known source: the משנה about a field improved during שביעית, together with the tradition in the next step.

steps.title: The son may plant the field, so the penalty was on the father only
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי ברבי חנינא has a tradition: if the father improved the field and died, his son may plant it. So the רבנן penalized only the father, not the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי ברבי חנינא said: We have a tradition that if he improved the field and then died, his son may sow it. This shows that the רבנן penalized him, the father, but did not penalize his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes his proof. A tradition says the son may plant the field, and the גמרא concludes that the קנס was on the man himself, not on his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קנס were on the field itself, it would stay even after the father died, and the son could not plant it. Since the son may plant it, the penalty must have been on the father as a person. This answers the question of step 16 in the same way for the man who slit the בכור's ear: his son is not penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a received tradition
He improved it (the field)
It follows that, apparently
Him himself
The רבנן imposed a penalty

steps.whatToRemember: The son may plant the field his father improved during שביעית, so this קנס is on the person, not the property. רבי זירא uses this to answer רבי ירמיה: the son of the man who slit a בכור's ear is not penalized.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main proof for the question of step 16. It shows the general way to tell whether a rabbinic penalty is on a person or on his property: check whether it passes on to the heir.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן,
phrases.english: And Rav Asi son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: We have a tradition:
If he improved it and died, his son may sow it.
Apparently, the Rabbis penalized him himself;
they did not penalize his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that began with the משנה in step 17 by adding רב אסי's tradition and drawing the conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: The question of step 16: is the קנס on the person or on his property?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית together with רב אסי ברבי חנינא's tradition that the son may sow the improved field.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן penalized the man himself, not his son, so the קנס ends when he dies.

steps.title: אביי begins a tradition of his own
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens with 'we have a tradition'. The content of his tradition comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement from אביי. Only the opening words appear here, and his actual tradition comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses the same opening, נקטינן, that רב אסי just used. This tells us he is adding another received tradition to the discussion. We cannot yet tell what it says or how it relates to רבי זירא's proof, so we wait for the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a leading אמורא in Babylonia

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new tradition after רבי זירא's proof. This is a setup line whose content follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This is only the opening of אביי's tradition.
